Get your laptop ready before Day 1. Plan **30–60 minutes** the day before — not the morning of. The optional [Day 0](Schedule.qmd#day-0-optional-software-setup-computational-refresher) session is the place to bring any install problems you can't solve yourself.

::: callout-tip
**What you'll have at the end:**

1. R and RStudio installed and working
2. VS Code installed
3. A workshop project (`scrnaseq_workshop`) created in RStudio

Installing the R / Bioconductor packages (plus LaTeX and a Quarto primer) is handled in **[Tutorial 00 — Get Up and Running with R, RStudio & Quarto](Exercise_Folder/Tutorial_00_Setup_RStudio_Packages.html)**, which we walk through together at the start of Day 1.
:::

## 1. Required tools

- **R ≥ 4.4** — [download](https://www.r-project.org)
- **RStudio Desktop** (current release) — [download](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/)
- **VS Code** (current release) — [download](https://code.visualstudio.com/download). We use VS Code during the workshop, so please install it ahead of time.

### Windows users — install WSL2 + Ubuntu

The command-line refresher (Day 0 / [Appendix B](Resources_Folder/Appendix_B_Unix_Command_Line.html)) assumes a POSIX shell. The simplest path on Windows is WSL2:

1. Run **PowerShell as Administrator**.
2. `wsl --install -d ubuntu` and press Enter. Restart when prompted.
3. Launch **Ubuntu** from the Start menu and set a username and password.
4. `sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade -y`

Full Microsoft guide: <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/install>

### Mac or Linux

Use the built-in **Terminal** app, or install [iTerm2](https://iterm2.com/) (Mac) for a nicer experience.

## 2. Create a workshop project

In **RStudio**: *File → New Project → New Directory → New Project*. Name it `scrnaseq_workshop`. Inside that directory create a `data/` folder. The expected layout is:

```
scrnaseq_workshop/
├── scrnaseq_workshop.Rproj
├── data/                    # any local datasets go here
└── tutorials/               # downloaded tutorial .qmd files
```

## 3. Install the R packages

The R / Bioconductor packages the workshop uses — along with a short primer on how packages, updates, LaTeX, and Quarto work — are covered in **[Tutorial 00 — Get Up and Running with R, RStudio & Quarto](Exercise_Folder/Tutorial_00_Setup_RStudio_Packages.html)**. We do it together at the very start of Day 1, but because the first install can take **20–60 minutes**, we recommend opening Tutorial 00 and running its install block *before* you arrive.

## Something didn't work?

The [FAQ](FAQ.qmd) documents the issues that come up most often: Mac compiler errors, `BiocManager` mirror selection, RStudio caching old library paths, etc.
